content:
The [JSON to CSV Converter](/json-to-csv-converter) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Convert JSON data to CSV — paste JSON, get a spreadsheet-ready file. Enter your JSON input and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Convert JSON data into CSV — the format spreadsheets and databases expect. Paste an array of objects (rows) and get back comma-separated values with a header row built from the object keys. Fields containing commas, quotes or new lines are quoted automatically, so the output opens cleanly in Excel, Google Sheets or any CSV reader. If the JSON has a syntax error, the tool says so instead of guessing. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the JSON to CSV Converter

Start by typing or pasting your JSON input. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste your JSON — an array of objects, or a single object.
2. Read the CSV output — the first row is the header.
3. Copy the output and paste it into a spreadsheet, or save it as a .csv file.

## How it works

The [JSON to CSV Converter](/json-to-csv-converter) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. An array of two objects — {"name": "Ana", "age": 30} and {"name": "Bilal", "age": 25} — becomes a CSV with the header “name,age” and two data rows. Try the same figures in the [JSON to CSV Converter](/json-to-csv-converter) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (JSON input: [ {"name": "Ana", "age": 30, "city": "Lahore"}, {"name": "Bilal", "age": 25, "city": "Karachi"} ]), the [JSON to CSV Converter](/json-to-csv-converter) returns CSV output: name,age,city Ana,30,Lahore Bilal,25,Karachi, Rows: 3 (including the header row), Status: Valid JSON. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [URL Encoder](/url-encoder) is worth a look before you finish.

## What JSON shape works

The tool expects an array of objects, where each object is one row and its keys are the columns — for example [{"name": "Ana", "age": 30}, {"name": "Bilal", "age": 25}]. A single object works too and becomes one data row. Nested objects and arrays are kept as JSON text inside the cell, so nothing is lost. A bare number, string or mixed array is rejected with a clear message.

## Quoting rules

CSV has one rule that matters: any field containing a comma, a quote or a new line must be wrapped in double quotes, and quotes inside it are doubled. The converter does this automatically — a name like “Ana, Jr.” becomes "Ana, Jr." and a quote becomes "". That is what lets Excel open the file without splitting fields in the wrong places.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Arrays of objects convert best — one object per row.
- Fields with commas or quotes are quoted automatically.
- Open the result in Excel or Google Sheets to check the columns.

## Frequently asked questions

### What JSON can I convert to CSV?

An array of objects (one object per row) or a single object. The keys become the column headers. Nested values are kept as JSON text inside the cell. Try it with your own numbers in the [JSON to CSV Converter](/json-to-csv-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How are commas inside values handled?

The field is wrapped in double quotes, so “Ana, Jr.” becomes "Ana, Jr." and the comma does not split the column. Quotes inside a field are doubled. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.

### Can I convert CSV back to JSON?

Yes — the CSV to JSON converter on this site does the reverse, with the first row as the headers. Try it with your own numbers in the [JSON to CSV Converter](/json-to-csv-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser — the JSON never leaves your device. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.
